threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: The way you stand on the corner of Church Street looking lost with a full shopping bag like it’s your first day at a new job.
Caught a glimpse of a guy arguing with a lamppost on the 3 bus last night. I swear I heard it say 'no more'. Ah, the joys of night travel.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I heard a neighbor serenading their cat in the park while prepping for a barbeque—only in Reuterkiez.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Prenzlauer Berg, it's normal to see prams parked outside cafes, almost like a second class of customers. Only in Berlin, really.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You'll notice locals are the ones who know the best taco spots and still tip big at the corner panaderia, even when it's packed.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a glimpse of a kid breakdancing in between cars on a packed 14 bus. Only in San Francisco do you get entertainment with your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars close early, but on weekends, the locals don’t even show up until midnight. It's a whole different vibe after hours.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You know they're new when they still call it 'Paseo de Gracia' instead of 'Passeig de Gràcia' and look confused when you mention 'el metro'.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the underground' and get confused when your train's a day late.
Last week, saw a bloke on the 59 who kept insisting he was the reincarnation of Churchill. Pushed the driver to let him make a speech at the next stop.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy juggling flaming torches on Karl-Marx-Straße while waiting for a delayed bus. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find wild squirrels raiding beer gardens, somehow knowing exactly when to appear for the leftover pretzels.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can always tell a long-time local by how they handle BART delays—calmly pull out a book instead of checking their phones.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in full formal attire juggling at the 16th St. BART, right next to a woman in sweats with a coffee. Only in San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the best food is in fancy restaurants; the real hidden gems are in the tiny takeaways tucked behind the main squares.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their enthusiasm for the Mercat de Gràcia, snapping photos of every stall while locals just grab their groceries.
